text: Q3 2025 Revenue Summary: Total revenue reached $42.8M, representing a 23% year-over-year increase. Enterprise contracts contributed $28.1M while self-serve accounted for $14.7M. The EMEA region drove the majority of growth with a 41% increase in new logo bookings. Customer churn decreased to 2.1% from 3.4% in the prior quarter, reflecting improved onboarding and product stickiness.

Infrastructure Cost Analysis FY2025: GPU compute spend totaled $8.4M across 10 cloud providers in 19 regions. B200 clusters accounted for 62% of spend but delivered 78% of inference throughput. Reserved capacity saved $1.9M versus on-demand pricing. Recommended actions: increase reserved B200 allocation by 15% and migrate EU inference traffic from region us-east-1 to eu-west-1 to reduce latency by 40ms.

Security Incident Report INC-2025-0847: On July 14, an unauthorized API key was detected making excessive requests to the model serving endpoint. The key was traced to a deprecated integration with the analytics pipeline. Immediate actions: key revocation, audit of all API keys older than 90 days, implementation of automatic key rotation every 60 days. No customer data was exposed. Root cause: missing deprecation workflow for service integrations.

Product Roadmap H2 2025: Priority initiatives include multi-LoRA serving for cost-efficient A/B testing of fine-tuned models, extended context support to 256K tokens for the Qwen3 family, and a managed training agent that automates dataset preparation through deployment. Secondary initiatives: vision-language model fine-tuning GA, DPO support for serverless training, and improved checkpoint resume for long-running RL jobs.

Customer Success Playbook - Enterprise Onboarding: Phase 1 (Week 1-2): Deploy base model, configure API access, run baseline evals on customer eval set. Phase 2 (Week 3-4): Collect 500-1000 domain examples, run SFT with LoRA rank 32-64, evaluate against baseline. Phase 3 (Week 5-6): Iterate on failure modes, expand dataset, retrain. Phase 4 (Week 7-8): Full-parameter CPT if domain gap is large, followed by SFT. Deploy to production with auto-scaling.

Model Evaluation Framework: All fine-tuned models must pass three evaluation gates before production deployment. Gate 1: Holdout perplexity within 10% of base model on general text (regression check). Gate 2: Domain-specific accuracy >= 85% on curated eval set. Gate 3: Safety evaluation with red-team prompts showing no degradation from base model. Models failing any gate are rolled back to the previous checkpoint and the training data is audited for contamination.

API Rate Limiting Policy: Free tier: 10 requests/minute, 1,000 requests/day. Pro tier: 60 requests/minute, 10,000 requests/day. Enterprise: custom limits with burst capacity up to 2x sustained rate. Rate limits are enforced per API key, not per IP. Token-based limits may be introduced in Q4 2025 for models with variable output lengths. All rate limit headers are included in API responses: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset.

Data Pipeline Architecture: Training data flows through five stages. Ingestion: raw data collected from customer uploads and internal sources. Validation: schema checks, PII scanning, deduplication. Rendering: chat template applied, tokenization, weight masking. Storage: versioned datasets in object storage with lineage tracking. Training: streaming data loader pulls from storage, renders on-the-fly in worker processes to keep memory O(workers) not O(dataset).

Pricing Model for Fine-Tuned Models: Base inference price is determined by the underlying model token pricing. LoRA adapter serving adds a 15% premium for multi-LoRA deployments and 25% for dedicated single-adapter deployments. Full-parameter fine-tuned models are priced at 1.5x base when deployed on dedicated GPUs. Training costs are separate: serverless at $0.50 per 1M tokens, dedicated at GPU-hour rates ranging from $4.50/hr (A100) to $12.00/hr (B200).

Incident Postmortem Template: 1. Summary: one-paragraph description of impact. 2. Timeline: UTC timestamps from detection to resolution. 3. Root cause: technical analysis with contributing factors. 4. Resolution: immediate fix and verification. 5. Action items: owned, tracked, with deadlines. 6. Lessons learned: what worked, what did not, process improvements. All postmortems are reviewed within 5 business days and action items are tracked to completion in the engineering tracker.
